document.abstract: This paper proposes a program production system over an IP network that uses and integrates Unique Material Identifier (UMID), Material eXchange Format (MXF), and non-destructive editing, based on the editing description. In this system, materials and their metadata on distributed servers can be accessed from anywhere on the network by attaching a UMID to all materials and by wrapping the UMID, metadata, and materials in MXF format The result of editing is output in the form of an editing description, and all materials are referred to by the UMID in the editing description. In broadcasting, or completing the program, the video reproduction equipment searches the original source material by the UMID and processes materials with effects according to the editing description. Images to be superimposed can be created in parallel while editing the program, by notifying the program producer application of the UMID only. The system has been implemented experimentally, its operation has been verified, and its effectiveness confirmed.

authors.bio: Shinya Takeuchi graduated from the University of Tokyo, Japan, in 1999 with a M.S. degree in electrical engineering. That same year, he joined NHK (Japan Broadcasting Corp.), where he was engaged in video engineering. Since 2002, he has worked at NHK Science and Technical Research Laboratories, where he is involved in networked broadcasting station systems.
authors.name: Shinya Takeuchi

authors.bio: Yutaka Kaneko received B.S. and M.S. degrees in electrical engineering from the University of Electro-Communications, Tokyo, Japan, in 1988 and 1990, respectively. In 1990, he joined NHK and since 1994 has worked at NHK Science and Technical Research Laboratories, where he is currently engaged in research on networked broadcasting station systems, image processing and motion picture coding. Kaneko is a member of ITE Japan, IEICE Japan, and IPS Japan.
authors.name: Yutaka Kaneko

authors.bio: Makoto Yamamoto received B.S. and M.S. degrees in communication engineering from Tohoku University, Sendai, Japan, in 1982 and 1984, respectively. In 1984, he joined NHK. Since 1987, he has worked at NHK Science and Technical Research Laboratories, where he is engaged in research on networked broadcasting station systems and optical transmission systems. Yamamoto is a member of ITE Japan.
authors.name: Makoto Yamamoto

authors.bio: Masahiro Shibata graduated in 1979 from the electronics department, Faculty of Engineering, Kyoto University, from which he also received a M.S. in 1981 and a Ph.D. in 2003. He joined NHK in 1981 and has been engaged in research and development on information retrieval technology, image database, and contents handling systems.
authors.name: Masahiro Shibata

authors.bio: Atsushi Narumi joined NHK in 1990, where he was involved in the operation of video editing and outside broadcast engineering. He transferred to the engineering administration development at NHK headquarters in 1998, developing digital video sever systems and NLE editing systems. He is currently involved in developing the HDTV video server system and HDTV NLE editing system. Narumi is P/FF chairman in ABU.
authors.name: Atsushi Narumi

authors.bio: Shunji Sunasaki joined NHK in 1986, where he was involved in the operation of video editing and outside broadcast engineering. He transferred to the engineering administration development at NHK headquarters in 1996, developing digital HDTV OB vans and other peripherals that can produce both HDTV and SDTV programs simultaneously. Since 2002, he has been involved in developing the HDTV streaming and file transmission system over TCP/IP networks at NHK Engineering Services, Inc.
authors.name: Shunji Sunasaki
